title: 10 Business Challenges Small Businesses Can’t Ignore In 2027
content:
The 2026 environment already demonstrates how complicated this can become. Federal tax changes affect areas including the Qualified Business Income deduction, overtime, and tips, while employment rules and state-level requirements continue to evolve.

The SBA is also considering proposed changes to its small business size standards. The August 2026 proposals would simplify many industry classifications and expand the number of firms qualifying under the federal definition of a small business. [...] Hiring challenges remain one of the biggest operational challenges for small businesses and will likely continue into 2027.

NFIB’s July 2026 survey showed that 36% of small business owners had job openings they could not fill, the highest reading since June 2025. [...] Growth can mean hiring, integrating new technology, adding inventory, expanding a location, expanding marketing, or entering a new market. Each decision can create new revenue opportunities while also increasing expenses and operational complexity. For small businesses, sustainable growth may therefore depend on understanding capacity before pursuing expansion.
